kit.name: Cultivarium JERBOA Toolkit (Jumping Element libRaries with Broad hOst rAnge)
kit.description: Cultivarium JERBOA Toolkit (Jumping Element libRaries with Broad hOst rAnge). Host: Broad host range - non-model bacteria; the vectors carry an RK2/RP4 oriT for conjugation and an R6K-gamma conditional origin so they cannot replicate in the recipient. Addgene kit #1000000275. Deposited by Nili Ostrov / Charlie Gilbert (Cultivarium). JERBOA uses NO named part syntax - not MoClo, not CIDAR, not PhytoBricks, not Marburg, not SEVA. It is a bespoke three-part BsaI scheme whose junctions are placed on the transposase and marker start codons, which is why the vector-to-transposase junction differs between the two families (CCAT for Himar1, TCAT for Tn5) while the other two junctions (CGTA where the two promoters meet back-to-back and divergent, AATG at the marker start) are shared. The two promoter parts are transcribed in opposite directions from the shared CGTA junction. The advertised 3,888 transposon variants is the combinatorial product 2 transposases x 6 antibiotic markers x 18 x 18 promoter combinations, not a count of plasmids; the kit itself holds 71 plasmids (18 Himar1 transposase-promoter + 18 Tn5 transposase-promoter + 23 marker-promoter + 12 destination vectors). The kit is intended for pooled high-throughput screening to find a working transposon configuration in a new host, so the practical unit is a library rather than a single designed construct.

kit.name: CyanoGate Kit
kit.description: CyanoGate Kit. Host: Cyanobacteria (Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803, Synechococcus elongatus PCC 7942, Synechococcus sp. UTEX 2973 and other strains). Addgene kit #1000000146. Deposited by Alistair J. McCormick (University of Edinburgh). CyanoGate is an extension of the plant MoClo / PhytoBrick standard and REQUIRES the MoClo Toolkit (Addgene kit #1000000044) for the level 0 and level 1 acceptor vectors. Assembly uses BsaI (Eco31I) and BpiI (=BbsI) only; no unsupported enzymes. The underlying PhytoBrick level 0 sub-position chain, read literally from Patron et al. 2015 (New Phytologist 208:13-19, the common-syntax table, open-access PDF at https://wrap.warwick.ac.uk/id/eprint/70164/3/WRAP_0581786-lf-140715-new_phytologist_viewpoint_patron_et_al.pdf), is: A1/DIST GGAG->TGAC, A2/PROX TGAC->TCCC, A3/CORE TCCC->TACT, A4/5UTR TACT->CCAT, B2/NTAG CCAT->AATG, B3/CDS1 AATG->AGGT (or AGCC), B4/CDS2 AGGT->TTCG, B5/CTAG TTCG->GCTT, B6/3UTR GCTT->GGTA, C1/TERM GGTA->CGCT. CyanoGate's own stated overhang pairs are all consistent with this chain, but CyanoGate itself only prints the coarser positions listed in the L1 level above, so the finer sub-positions are recorded here as a note rather than as CyanoGate slots. Level T vectors come in replicative (RSF1010- and RK2-based) and integrative (pUC19-based, sacB counter-selection) sub-types.

kit.description: EMMA - Extensible Mammalian Modular Assembly Toolkit. Host: Mammalian cells. Addgene kit #1000000119. Deposited by Yizhi Cai (University of Edinburgh; work with Steven M. Pollard). Enzyme assignment is the reverse of the common assumption: EMMA's main one-pot assembly of parts into the ccdB receiver vector uses BsmBI, and BsaI is reserved for the optional second-step (multigene) assembly via the four dedicated BsaI connectors (Addgene #100668-#100671, named HC_Kan_conn_BsaI-1_p1, BsaI-2_p24, BsaI-3_p1, BsaI-4_p25). kit.description: Golden GATEway Cloning Kit. Host: E. coli cloning; transgenesis constructs demonstrated in zebrafish (Danio rerio); Gateway destination vectors make it portable to other model organisms. Addgene kit #1000000054. Deposited by Joachim Wittbrodt (Centre for Organismal Studies, Heidelberg University). Only the FIRST of the kit's two cloning steps is Type IIS. The paper: 'For the Golden Gate cloning step, we use up to eight different entry vectors per reaction. These entry vectors represent eight consecutive positions in the assembled DNA element. The positions are defined via the overhangs that are created using BsaI restriction digest.' The SECOND step is Multisite Gateway attL/attR recombination with LR Clonase II Plus, not a Type IIS reaction, so it is not modelled as a level here. Combined depth: 'This approach allows the assembly of a maximum of 24 fragments (3 (Multisite Gateway) x 8 (Golden Gate)).' An assembly always starts at position 1 and may stop at any position n by using the primed variant pGGEV_n', whose downstream overhang is TAAG. DESTINATION-VECTOR CAVEAT: no fetched document prints the destination vector's own overhangs in a table. The paper says 'two different destination vectors exist with adjusted 5' overhangs' and 'The 3' overhang of the destination vector contains an in-frame stop codon'; combined with Table 1 this makes ATGG (or GTAT) and TAAG the vector-to-insert junctions, but that is derived rather than literally read. Addgene data error: the kit page's reference block prints a second DOI, 10.1371/journal.pone.0083043, immediately after the correct one. That DOI is PMID 24376629, the unrelated GreenGate plant cloning paper (Lampropoulos et al.), and must not be ingested as a Golden GATEway citation.

kit.name: GoldenBraid 2.0 Kit
kit.description: GoldenBraid 2.0 Kit. Host: Plants (Nicotiana benthamiana, Arabidopsis thaliana, etc.); binary T-DNA vectors for Agrobacterium-mediated transformation. Addgene kit #1000000076. Deposited by Diego Orzaez (IBMCP, CSIC-UPV, Valencia). Levels needing an unsupported enzyme or lacking a verified overhang table: Level 0 domestication into pUPD / pUPD2 (BsmBI); Level omega MULTIPARTITE assembly directly from pUPD parts (BtgZI/BsmBI reaction) (BtgZI). GoldenBraid is a 'double loop': alpha-level destination plasmids (pDGB-alpha1/alpha2, plus reverse-orientation alpha1R/alpha2R) are opened with BsaI and, once filled, are flanked by BsmBI sites; omega-level plasmids (pDGB-Omega1/Omega2/1R/2R) are opened with BsmBI and, once filled, are flanked by BsaI sites. Three-tier GoldenMOCS-derived system: BB1 (BsaI) for single parts, BB2 (BpiI = BbsI) for one transcription unit, BB3 (BsaI) for up to eight units. The four part-level fusion sites are Fs1=GGAG, Fs2=CATG (contains the ATG start codon), Fs3=GCTT, Fs4=CGCT; the transcription-unit-level fusion sites are FsA=GATC, FsB=CCGG, FsC=AATT, FsD=AGCT, FsE=GGAG, FsF=GCTT, FsG=CGCT, FsH=CAAC, FsI=TGGT. kit.description: MoChlo: Modular Cloning Chloroplast Toolbox. Host: Plastid (chloroplast) genome of tobacco (Nicotiana tabacum) and potato (Solanum tuberosum). Addgene kit #1000000156. kit.name: MoClo Yeast Toolkit (YTK)
kit.description: MoClo Yeast Toolkit (YTK). Host: Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Addgene kit #1000000061. Deposited by John E. Dueber lab. Enzyme order verified in the paper itself: source DNA is 'domesticated via BsmBI' into a part plasmid, part plasmids carry 'unique upstream and downstream BsaI-generated overhangs', one part of each Type is 'assembled using BsaI to form a cassette plasmid', and cassettes 'can be further assembled using BsmBI to form a multigene plasmid' (Figure 1 caption). The full ring closes: Type 8 -> CCCT -> Type 1. Composite parts exist and were confirmed in the same bundle: pYTK047 GFP dropout (type 234r, GCTG->AACG i.e. reverse-oriented AACG->GCTG), pYTK048/049 spacers (AACG->GCTG), pYTK095 (678, TACA->CCCT) and pYTK096 (pre-assembled URA3 integration vector, GCTG->AACG). Level 0 part flanks: a part insert carries TCGG at its 5' end and GACC at its 3' end; the TCGG fusion site regenerates the GGTCTC (BsaI) site in the finished part plasmid. NotI is used for vector linearisation only, not for assembly. The paper's own part-type table lives in the ACS Supporting Information, which returns HTTP 403 to automated fetches; the overhangs above were therefore read off the depositor's GenBank files rather than that table, and they are mutually consistent across all 96 plasmids.

kit.name: MultiGreen
kit.description: MultiGreen. Host: Plants (multi-gene plant transformation constructs). Addgene kit #1000000250. Deposited by Wayne A. Parrott (University of Georgia). MultiGreen is an architecture layered ON TOP of GreenGate, not a new fusion-site grammar. Two multiplexing routes: (1) MultiGreen 1.0, multiplexing in SERIES, introduces the optional H overhang by splitting the FG position into new Level 0 FH (transcription blocker) and HG (multiplexer) entry vectors; the HG module carries a pair of Esp3I (BsmBI) sites internal to its BsaI sites but external to a chromoprotein reporter, so successive rounds can be screened by alternating visual reporters. The original GreenGate H overhang is TAGG (Lampropoulos 2013 Fig 4 caption) but MultiGreen does not reprint it, so H is not enumerated as a slot here. (2) MultiGreen 2.0, multiplexing in PARALLEL, uses 12 level 1 intermediary destination vectors each holding one of the AB/BC/CD/DE/EF/FG overhang pairs; a level 1 assembly is done with BsaI plus Esp3I in the same cocktail, where Esp3I frees the receptive A-G destination overhangs for the next round. Kit contents per Addgene: 12 intermediate destination vectors, 3 final destination vectors, 7 MultiGreen 1.0 expanded entry vectors, 20 linker modules, 6 empty entry vectors (48 plasmids). Both BsaI and Esp3I are in the supported set.

kit.description: Multiplex Yeast Toolkit (MYT). Host: Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Addgene kit #1000000229. Deposited by Tom Ellis lab. kit.name: OpenPlant Kit (Loop assembly)
kit.description: OpenPlant Kit (Loop assembly). Host: Marchantia polymorpha (also used in Arabidopsis thaliana and Anthoceros agrestis); includes Marchantia chloroplast transformation vectors. Addgene kit #1000000272. Deposited by Jim Haseloff (University of Cambridge) / OpenPlant. Levels needing an unsupported enzyme or lacking a verified overhang table: Level 0 part cloning into pUAP4 (universal acceptor plasmid) (SapI). 79 plasmids. Loop assembly alternates BsaI (odd levels L1/L3/...) and SapI (even levels L2/L4/...) so that the product of one level is the substrate of the next; only four odd receivers and four even receivers are ever needed. Odd receivers are kanamycin resistant, even receivers spectinomycin resistant, which is what makes one-pot selection work. In this kit the odd receivers are pCk1-4 (and pCk1-4chlo for chloroplast work) and the even receivers are pCsA, pCsB, pCsC, pCsE (and pCsA/B/C/Echlo) - note the even receivers are named after the BsaI overhang letter they start at (A, B, C, E), while the odd receivers are numbered after their SapI position. Spacer plasmids (pCk1-4_spacer, pCsA/B/C/E_spacer) fill unused positions when fewer than four modules are assembled. Every level uses only BsaI or SapI, both supported; the only caveat is that SapI gives 3-base overhangs.

kit.description: Phytobrick / Plant Common Syntax (Type IIS standard for plant DNA parts). Host: Plants (standard is host-agnostic; designed for eukaryotic transcriptional units). kit.description: Ralstonia-GG-Kit. Host: Ralstonia solanacearum species complex (Rssc); modules are cross-compatible with the plant 'plant-GG-kit'. Addgene kit #1000000142. Deposited by Thomas Lahaye (University of Tuebingen). Levels needing an unsupported enzyme or lacking a verified overhang table: Knockout-construct branch (upstream flank + marker + downstream flank -> LII destination) (BsaI). 17 plasmids, Addgene #104514-#104530. All enzymes are supported: BsaI (Eco31I) for level I to II and for the knockout branch, BpiI (=BbsI) for level II to III. kit.name: Start-Stop Assembly Toolkit
kit.description: Start-Stop Assembly Toolkit. Host: Escherichia coli (core vectors built on pUC19, pACYC177, pACYC184; framework is organism-agnostic). Addgene kit #1000000152. Deposited by John T. Heap (Imperial College London); George M. Taylor, Pawel M. Mordaka. IMPORTANT: Level 1 uses SapI (GCTCTTC(1/4)), which leaves a THREE-base overhang, not four. The three-base sites are alpha=CAG, beta=CCA, gamma=ATG (the start codon), delta=TAA (the stop codon), epsilon=GGA - this is what makes the CDS junctions functionally scarless. Isoschizomers of SapI are LguI and BspQI. Levels 2 and 3 use ordinary 4-base overhangs and reuse sequences from the published MoClo/CIDAR sets. With fewer than 5 expression units, the last unit is built in a 'Z vector' (pStA1AZ, pStA1BZ, pStA1CZ, pStA1DZ, pStA1EZ) so that the level-2 acceptor pair is always A/Z; that is why a single level-2 vector serves any unit count. pStA313 accepts 2 level-2 constructs (acceptor TGCC/TTAC), pStA314 accepts 3 (acceptor TGCC/CGAG). Parts must contain no internal SapI, BsaI or BbsI sites.

kit.name: T2A Split/Link TurboID Kit
kit.description: T2A Split/Link TurboID Kit. Host: Mammalian cells (transient transfection, piggyBac transposition or lentiviral transduction). Addgene kit #1000000249. Deposited by Sven Eyckerman (VIB-UGent Center for Medical Biotechnology, Ghent University). The kit page states the lineage verbatim: 'The T2A Split/Link TurboID Kit is a sequential Golden Gate assembly method originally based on the GreenGate and Golden GATEway assembly kits', and the Level-0 module vectors are 'provided by the GreenGate kit'. Three levels of hierarchy, two of them Type IIS: Level-0 modules (BsaI-flanked basic parts, overhangs A to G) assemble into Level-1 transcription units, and two Level-1 TUs assemble into a Level-2 vector (BsmBI, overhangs W, X, Z). Level-0, Level-1 and Level-2 backbones all carry a ccdB toxin gene between the enzyme sites under a lacUV5 promoter for negative selection; Level-0 and Level-2 confer carbenicillin/ampicillin resistance while Level-1 confers kanamycin, so lower-order plasmids cannot be selected at the next level. Level 2 is fixed at exactly two transcription units - there is no connector series for more. Ready-made Level-1 marker TUs (puromycin, blasticidin, neomycin, hygromycin) are supplied for both piggyBac and lentiviral routes.

kit.description: The Mammalian Toolkit (MTK). Host: Mammalian cells. Addgene kit #1000000180. Deposited by Hana El-Samad (University of California, San Francisco). Enzyme roles, verbatim from the Bio-protocol article: part domestication into the chloramphenicol-resistant part vector uses BsmBI (FastDigest Esp3I); TU assembly uses BsaI-HFv2; multi-TU assembly into the Part 0 destination vector uses Esp3I (BsmBI). Part 8a fwd CCGA / Part 8b fwd CAAT, so the 8a->8b junction is CAAT and 8b still ends at CCCT. Two other rows of the same table - Part 4b reverse 'CAGC' and Part 234 reverse 'CAGC' - both reverse-complement to GCTG. The Part 4 -> Part 5 junction is therefore recorded here as GCTG (literally read as Part 5's forward overhang) and 'CGAC' is treated as a typo in the published table. MULTI-TU SLOT ORDER: Table 2 lists each connector pair (Ln, Rn) sharing one overhang, plus LS and RE. The article confirms LS sits on Part 1 (5' end of a TU) and RE on Part 5 (3' end), and that 'L1 connects with R1', giving: destination vector -> LS (CTGA) -> TU1 -> R1/L1 (CCAA) -> TU2 -> ... -> R8/L8 (TTTA) -> final TU -> RE (AGCA) -> back to the vector. In an n-TU assembly only LS, R1..R(n-1) and RE are used, so the slot list here is the maximal 9-TU case. UNRESOLVED: the Part 4a -> Part 4b junction. Table 1 gives Part 4a reverse 'GCCA' (reverse complement TGGC) but Part 4b forward 'TCGG'; these disagree and no second source in the fetched documents resolves it, so no 4a/4b junction overhang is reported

kit.name: XanthoMoClo Xanthobacter Genetic Toolkit
kit.description: XanthoMoClo Xanthobacter Genetic Toolkit. Host: Xanthobacter spp. and Roseixanthobacter spp. (validated across 23 strains / 21 species), plus E. coli. Addgene kit #1000000259. Deposited by Michael Springer (Harvard Medical School). STRUCTURALLY UNUSUAL: XanthoMoClo is a single-level, one-pot, VECTORLESS system. There is no destination vector - the twelve part positions ligate into a complete circle by themselves, with Part Types 1 and 2 serving as the E. coli backbone. Tooling that assumes 'N parts plus one destination vector' needs a special case here. The last slot listed (Part Type 0, oriT) is the one that closes the circle. Ten skip-linkers let a build omit positions: L1 AACG->GAGT (skips PT5-11), L2 GCTG->GAGT (skips PT8-11), L3 TACA->GAGT (skips PT11), L4 GCTG->TACA (skips PT8-10), L5 AACG->TACA (skips PT5-10), L6 CCCT->AACG (skips PT3-4), L7 CCCT->TGGC (skips PT3), L8 TGGC->AACG (skips PT4), L9 GAGT->CCGA (skips PT0), L10 GCTG->CCGA (skips PT8 through PT0) - all from Supplementary Table 2 and all confirmed in the GenBank scan. Multi-position parts exist too: pXTK015 SacB spans PT5-7 (AACG->GCTG) and pXTK016 SacB spans PT8-10 (GCTG->TACA). NOTE the deliberate asymmetry TATG (PT5->PT6) versus AATG (PT8->PT9): cassette 1 and cassette 2 coding-sequence parts are NOT interchangeable. PaqCI is NOT an assembly enzyme in this kit - it appears only in plasmid names such as 'PaqCI-Compatible' (pXTK146-149, pXTK-BB5/BB6/BB7), meaning those variants have been domesticated for users doing PaqCI work elsewhere. No AarI, BtgZI or SapI anywhere. Documentation bugs worth not propagating: Supporting Information 1 writes 'the BsaI recognition site (CGTCTC(N)1)' - CGTCTC is BsmBI, BsaI is GGTCTC, and the 160 GenBank files confirm GGTCTC flanks every part; and its prose misdescribes

kit.name: Yarrowia lipolytica Golden Gate tool kit
kit.description: Yarrowia lipolytica Golden Gate tool kit. Host: Yarrowia lipolytica. Addgene kit #1000000167. Deposited by Tristan Rossignol / Jean-Marc Nicaud (INRAE, Micalis, Jouy-en-Josas). A flat, single-level 13-element BsaI assembly (no hierarchy): everything - integration flanks, marker, three promoter/gene/terminator units and the destination vector - goes into one pot. Fewer transcription units are built by using 'hybrid' terminators that jump positions: a terminator amplified with the E overhang forward and the L overhang reverse collapses positions E..L into one part (one transcription unit), and H-forward/L-reverse collapses H..L (two units). kit.name: Yeast GoldenBraid Cloning System and Toolkit
kit.description: Yeast GoldenBraid Cloning System and Toolkit. Host: Saccharomyces cerevisiae (W303, CEN.PK); genome integration at the YPRCdelta15 and YORWdelta22 LTR loci. Addgene kit #1000000138. Deposited by Elena Caro (deposited via Addgene; work from CBGP/UPM with the Orzaez GoldenBraid standard). Levels needing an unsupported enzyme or lacking a verified overhang table: Level 0 domestication into pUPD / pUPD2 (BsmBI). 27 plasmids: 4 vectors for YPRCdelta15 integration, 4 for YORWdelta22, 9 promoters, 8 mitochondrial targeting signals, an 8xHis N-terminal tag and resistance cassettes. I-SceI is a homing endonuclease used for linearisation, NOT a Golden Gate assembly enzyme, so it does not make any level unsupported. All assembly levels use only BsaI and BsmBI and are supported.

kit.name: Yeast Secrete and Detect
kit.description: Yeast Secrete and Detect. Host: Saccharomyces cerevisiae and Komagataella phaffii (Pichia pastoris). Addgene kit #1000000166. Deposited by Sylvestre Marillonnet lab (deposited); toolkit developed with the Martin J. Weissenborn lab. This kit does NOT use the YTK grammar. It follows the plant/universal MoClo syntax of Weber and Marillonnet: BbsI puts modules into the universal Level 0 acceptor pAGM9121, and BsaI builds the expression cassette. The fusion sites in the cassette are AATG (start codon), AGCA (a custom signal-peptide/protein junction introduced by this system), TTCG (protein/C-tag junction) and GCTT (stop codon), with AACG upstream of the promoter. The acceptor plasmids pPAP001-004 additionally carry a BbsI pair with fusion sites AACG and TACA, which brackets the whole promoter-to-tag transcription unit and appears to allow the unit to be moved between backbones; that level was not characterised further. pAGT572_Nemo carries a separate BbsI pair (TGCC/GCAA).

kit.name: yeast Tunable Expression Systems Toolkit (yTEST)
kit.description: yeast Tunable Expression Systems Toolkit (yTEST). Host: Saccharomyces cerevisiae. Addgene kit #1000000266. Deposited by Jeff Hasty lab. yTEST is a YTK-grammar part collection for five small-molecule-inducible promoter systems. Its one departure from stock YTK is a split promoter position: a Type 2a part runs AACG->TTGA and a Type 2b part runs TTGA->TATG, so the operator array and the core promoter can be mixed and matched. Only the 2a half (pRO232, pRO286) appears in this kit's plasmid set; the TTGA->TATG half is confirmed in the Ellis Yeast GPCR-sensor Toolkit, which uses the same junction. The publication is not open access, so all overhangs here were read from the depositor's sequences rather than from a table in the paper.
